slides.say: Two friends list the movies they watched this year. One lists thirty-four movies and the other lists twenty-seven. Together, their lists show forty-five different movies. How many movies appear on both lists?

So they ask for both, the movies on both lists. The hard part here isn't the math. It's one fact that isn't written in the question. We'll solve it in two different ways, by understanding, and then with the squares method.
Let's start by understanding the forty-five, like the stamps in the lesson. They didn't say forty-five movies came out this year. They said the two lists show forty-five different movies.
at: They said the two lists show

slides.say: So every one of the forty-five movies is on at least one list. No movie is on neither list. So neither is zero.
It's not written, but it comes from the words. Here the total is only the movies on the lists.
The first friend lists thirty-four of the forty-five movies. So forty-five minus thirty-four, eleven movies are not on the first list.

slides: Those eleven movies are still on a list, so they're on the second list only.

slides.say: The second list has twenty-seven movies, and eleven are only on the second list. So twenty-seven minus eleven, sixteen are on both lists.
And careful, eleven is choice number two. That's the second list only, not both. Choice number one is our answer.
at: Choice number one is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the math way, the squares method. We start again from the givens. We draw four boxes. Neither, second only, both, and first only. All four together are the forty-five different movies.
The first list covers both and first only, thirty-four. The second list covers second only and both, twenty-seven.
The forty-five counts only the movies on the lists, so no movie is on neither. The first box is zero.
Neither plus second only is everything outside the first list. That's forty-five minus thirty-four, eleven. And neither is zero, so second only is eleven.
The second list is twenty-seven. So both is twenty-seven minus eleven, sixteen.
And with counting each movie once, thirty-four plus twenty-seven is sixty-one. Sixty-one minus forty-five is sixteen. Those sixteen movies were counted twice.
Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number one is our answer
